title: Time pressure and plans to continue from 1926
summary: Albert regrets the short time, proposes a future session starting from 1926 when he left with Herschel Evans, and mentions Texas musicians nobody has interviewed. He faces a 600-mile drive with his daughter.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: We have Ollie Ross and Texas Tommy in your own band. Are there any ones you particularly want to hear or work on?

Well the time is so short Dick. I'm sorry it was like this. I most certainly want to spend some more time. Yeah well there'll be other trips. Yeah I understand. I would like to start next time from the beginning when I started and bring up some of the incidents that happened along with the big band that I had. Even with some going back to 1926 when I first left here with Herschel Evans as an alto player. Yeah.
I'd love to fill in all the details.

I surely would. I believe it's a great thing to fill in because there are a lot of good stories that are connected. where as you start this then you can go into some of the other great Texas musicians that played in those days. There were a lot of good ones. Why they're in the background? I don't know. I don't guess there's been anyone to interview them and discuss these things with them. Most of these fellas are dead.

Well I've been trying to work that out. But I'd like to play a little bit of your own band. All right. We'll go ahead. If you've got time for another one. I'm probably just going to take it as it comes on the LP for as long as you have time.
Well I think we're going to spend about 10 more minutes anyhow and we should get something. And I'd hate to rush off but we have these 600 miles looking at us.
Excuse me. Can you start? Yeah. It's on. It's set up now. The racket. Okay.
Yeah I know you've got a long trip in your... It's 600 miles. Yeah. Well I have a little help. My daughter's with me. She'll help me to drive some.
